clue.text: Selfish affection shown by skeletons secretly embracing?

definitions.text: Selfish affection shown by skeletons secretly embracing?

parts.words: Selfish affection shown by skeletons secretly embracing?
parts.note: skeletons proverbially hide in a closet for kitchen crockery, so their secret embrace is fondness of that storage place; the phrase also means fondness shown only for what one can get, like food

explanation.surface: Skeletons hugging in secret are accused of self-interested affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Skeletons proverbially hide in the cupboard, so their hidden hugging is love in a cupboard; the phrase means pretended affection shown in hope of gain, originally a child's fondness for whoever keeps the food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names pretended fondness offered only for the sake of food or other gain, which is selfish affection.

clue.text: Small boy and sister get a metal frame

parts.note: Chas is a short form of the boy's name Charles

explanation.surface: A little boy and his sister are given a metal frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The base framework of a car or other vehicle is its chassis, usually made of steel.

clue.text: River deity directly opposite

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A river god stands exactly across from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar opposites are as far apart as possible, like the two poles of the earth.

clue.text: Nothing bent, as it becomes inflexible

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: becomes signals that the letters of 'bent, as it' turn into something new

explanation.surface: Something unbending, once bent, grows stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the material; 'becomes' is what signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person refuses to change their mind, so obstinate means unbending.

clue.text: King dethroned by the rabble

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
a dethroned ruler is out of power

explanation.surface: A king is toppled by the mob.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the word is a disorderly crowd or mob, a rabble.

clue.text: Plan to take in Jack, the idle fellow

indicators.note: to take in means the plan word encloses the sailor

parts.note: a layout is a plan or arrangement
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A scheme to recruit Jack, who never does a stroke of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer who avoids work is a lazy, idle fellow.

clue.text: A sign giving the Roman male his marching orders?

parts.note: vir is Latin for man
to tell someone to go is to give them marching orders

explanation.surface: A sign that a Roman man is being sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' and 'his' just join the pieces; Latin VIR plus GO gives the sign of the zodiac whose name means virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Bet is right with one or more at the front

parts.note: an ante is a stake in poker
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A wager that one or more will be right at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' does no work beyond making the surface read naturally; OR is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior is the anatomical word for positioned forward, nearer the front.

clue.text: Cancel the campanologists' encore?

definitions.meaning: to revoke or annul, as with a law
bell-ringers' repeat performance would be a peal again

explanation.surface: Calling off the bell-ringers' repeat performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers, who ring peals; the pun splits the answer as RE-PEAL, a peal rung again.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a law is to annul it; split as re-peal it is a fresh ringing of bells.

clue.text: Where ducks are organized by rule, say?

indicators.note: organized means the letters of the three following words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Ducks seem to be kept in order by some rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' rearranges the letters of BY RULE SAY. AYLESBURY in Buckinghamshire, an English county, gives its name to a famous white breed of duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buckinghamshire market town is home of a classic white table duck breed, so it is a place for ducks.

clue.text: Cook used this compass

definitions.meaning: a kitchen stove with several burners and an oven
scope or extent, the reach of something

explanation.surface: A chef used this instrument for finding directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking stove and the full extent or scope of something share the one word.

clue.text: A big effort to provide a little music

definitions.meaning: a great exertion or stretch of strength

explanation.surface: Producing even a scrap of music takes a huge exertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hard exertion and a snatch of tune, as in the strains of a song.

clue.text: To be mad about fish is outmoded

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the fish
mad suggests the letters of 'To be' are thrown into a crazy new order

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Being crazy about fish is old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns TO BE into OBTE, and 'about' wraps those letters around SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer in use or fashion is out of date, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Scotland's Long Island sent back a message

indicators.note: sent back means the two joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: lang is the Scots word for long

explanation.surface: A message has been returned from Long Island, Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland has a real Long Island (a name for the Outer Hebrides), which disguises the Scots word for long; 'sent back' turns the whole joined pair round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign or communication sent to convey information is a message, a synonym.

clue.text: Faces forbidding services

parts.note: grim means stern and forbidding
aces are unreturnable serves in tennis

explanation.surface: Stern-looking church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' suggests church, but it is tennis, where an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisted expressions of disgust or pain are wry faces, as in pulling faces.

clue.text: Badly out in test of academic instruction

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: badly means the letters of 'out' are put in a poor new order

explanation.surface: Doing badly in a test of what one has been taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the word out, and 'in' places the result inside the test word; 'of' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A session of teaching given by a tutor to a small group or one student is academic instruction.

clue.text: Brute torn in pieces in the battle

indicators.note: in pieces means the letters of brute torn are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A savage is ripped apart during the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: OTTERBURN in Northumberland, northern England, was the site of a 1388 battle between the English and the Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1388 Anglo-Scottish clash, celebrated in ballad, took its name from the Northumberland village, a specific battle.

clue.text: Swimmer's fast speed coming up, difficult to follow

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the speed word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a fast clip is a rapid pace
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A swimmer's fast pace rises, hard to keep up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses the speed word, as befits a down clue, and 'to follow' puts the difficult word after it. The swimmer is a fish, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Touchstone a terribly erratic one of these?

definitions.text: Touchstone a terribly erratic one of these?

indicators.note: terribly means the letters of erratic, with one added, are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A touchstone that behaves erratically is a poor standard to judge by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges ERRATIC plus I. A touchstone is a standard of judgement, one example of what the plural answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards used for judging are criteria, and a touchstone is one such test.

clue.text: Not much change in the laundry

definitions.meaning: a large boiler once used in laundries for washing clothes

explanation.surface: Only a little loose money is left in the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain coppers are the small bronze coins, and a copper was also the big boiler for laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze small coins are coppers, and so was a washhouse boiler originally made of that metal.

clue.text: Amber needs this stiffener going before Tudor court

definitions.text: Amber needs this stiffener going before Tudor court

parts.words: Amber needs this stiffener going before Tudor court
parts.note: a laundry stiffener placed in front of the word amber spells the name of a notorious Tudor and Stuart law court

explanation.surface: Amber needs something to stiffen her resolve before appearing in a Tudor court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star Chamber was an English court of the Tudor and Stuart era; split differently it is the answer followed by AMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is the substance used to stiffen collars and linen, a stiffener.

clue.text: Sneaky-looking sequel to Toby's denigration

definitions.meaning: from the proverb 'give a dog a bad name and hang him': Toby is the dog in Punch and Judy

explanation.surface: Someone looking shifty after Toby's reputation is blackened.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby is the dog in the Punch and Judy puppet show; the proverb says a dog given a bad name will be hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A guilty, cowed expression is hangdog; following the proverb, denigrating a dog leads to hanging it.

clue.text: What perfects the career of a professional man?

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that repeated exercise makes perfect

definitions.text: the career of a professional man?
definitions.meaning: the business of a doctor or lawyer

explanation.surface: Asking what makes a professional man's career complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated rehearsal, as in the proverb, and a doctor's or lawyer's business both use this word.

clue.text: Short drink a pound, some say

definitions.note: some, said aloud, is sum, which means an aggregate amount

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
L stands for libra, the pound

explanation.surface: A small drink costs a pound, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken: 'some, say' is the sound of 'sum', meaning the whole amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the whole amount when figures are added together, a synonym.

clue.text: Hard worker in' Paris for example

definitions.meaning: one who works like a ... works hard
Paris was a prince of Troy in Greek legend

explanation.surface: Someone working hard in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris looks like the French capital but is the prince of Troy who abducted Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who toils tirelessly is said to work like a Trojan, and Paris was a son of King Priam of Troy.

clue.text: Genesis portrayed by namesake of its smooth man

definitions.text: Genesis portrayed by namesake of its smooth man

parts.words: Genesis portrayed by namesake of its smooth man
parts.note: the sculptor of the 1931 statue Genesis shares his first name with the smooth-skinned twin of hairy Esau in the Book of Genesis

explanation.surface: An artist depicting the first book of the Bible shares a name with one of its characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Esau was hairy and his twin brother smooth; the sculptor Jacob Epstein made a famous statue called Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriarch who tricked Esau and the sculptor Epstein share this first name.

clue.text: Bird's speed over the water

definitions.meaning: a nautical mile per hour, the unit of a ship's speed

explanation.surface: A bird's pace as it flies across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpiper-like wader and the sailor's unit of speed share one name.

clue.text: Katisha was the Mikado's daughter-in-law —

parts.note: the dash asks for the word completing Katisha's title in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta, meaning chosen but not yet installed

explanation.surface: A fact about Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado, Katisha is described as the daughter-in-law elect, the intended bride of the Mikado's son Nanki-Poo.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed after a title, the word means chosen for a role but not yet in it, as in president-elect.

clue.text: Girl putting on weight beginning to diet, it is declared

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a unit of weight

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of diet is taken

explanation.surface: A girl gaining weight just as her diet starts, it is revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting on' simply joins the pieces in order; 'it is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made known publicly has been proclaimed, a synonym.

clue.text: This pact, we hear, by a Liberal statesman?

definitions.text: This pact, we hear, by a Liberal statesman?

parts.words: This pact, we hear, by a Liberal statesman?
parts.note: pact sounds like packed, so this is a case one packs, named after the Victorian Liberal prime minister

explanation.surface: A treaty reportedly made by a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: William Gladstone was a Victorian Liberal prime minister; a hinged leather travel case was named after him, and 'pact, we hear' suggests something packed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian hinged leather travelling case bears the statesman's surname, so it is something to be packed.
